male.name: Puttaswamy
male.tagline: A Mandya cane and paddy farmer one bad season away from serious debt.

dayInLife.text: Walks his two cows to graze and checks the inlet channel watering the paddy nursery.
Works the field with Rathnamma, who does most transplanting and weeding; he manages irrigation turns and pesticide.
At cane harvest he also arranges migrant cane-cutting gangs for his own and neighbouring farms.
Between transplanting and harvest, the fortnightly dairy cooperative milk cheque is the only predictable income.
While waiting on the mill, he borrows from a cooperative society, then a private moneylender.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Life runs on canal water, cane cycles and delayed mill payments
points: Rises before 5 a.m. for the cows and the paddy nursery inlet, then works the field.
Mills routinely delay payment for crushed cane, so he borrows first from a cooperative society, then a moneylender.
A poor monsoon or a Cauvery release order to Tamil Nadu can cut his second paddy crop altogether.

stat.label: Rough annual cash income after diesel, fertiliser and labour costs

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Three generations share a small, already-divided holding
points: His 2.5 acres are half of what his father farmed before it was divided with his elder brother.
Rathnamma milks the cows, cooks for six, transplants and weeds, and cares for his ageing parents almost alone.
Puttaswamy, his father and his brother jointly decide on education and marriage; property is in his father's name.

stat.label: His land, half of what his father once farmed

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Daughter may continue to college by bus; son risks leaving at harvest
points: Puttaswamy left school after the seventh standard and does not want that repeated for his children.
Chaitra has just cleared SSLC; free Shakti bus travel to Malavalli, ten kilometres away, could decide PU college.
Kiran stays in school at harvest because Puttaswamy hires labour, but a bad cane-payment year could change that.

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Distance, debt stress and field hazards shape health
points: The family uses the village primary health centre, then Mandya hospital, with Mysuru for surgery or specialist care.
Sickle cuts, pesticide spray without reliable protective equipment and standing in flooded paddy are his main physical risks.
Rathnamma visits the health centre only when illness disrupts work; a hospitalisation worries him more than a bad monsoon.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Vokkaliga farming life anchored in temples, cooperative and caste networks
points: The family attends the Vairamudi festival at Melukote's Cheluvanarayana Swamy temple most years, and Chamundeshwari Temple at Dasara.
At peak transplanting and harvest he hires Scheduled Caste day labourers, most often Holeya.
His social world runs through the farmers' cooperative, mutual-aid networks and village-deity festivals, more than reservation politics.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Mills, canal water and revenue offices decide his fortunes
points: He joins protests outside mill gates, loosely under the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, when cane arrears stretch too long.
His household holds an Anna Bhagya Priority Household ration card, and he has taken MGNREGA work in two lean seasons.
His land records are on Bhoomi, yet he twice visited the taluk office to correct a survey-number discrepancy.

stat.label: Interim Cauvery release for fifteen days after the August 2023 standoff

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Proud of Mandya's sugar bowl, wary of mills and state priorities
points: He is proud of the KRS dam and Visvesvaraya's legacy, but feels the state treats agrarian distress as secondary.
He blames Cauvery release orders for failed paddy crops and the sugar mills for payment delays; he backs Mekedatu.
He wants Chaitra to finish PU college and Kiran to inherit the farm only after secondary school.

schoolPressures.label: Harvest labour
schoolPressures.detail: Cane-cutting season pulls neighbours' sons out of school; Kiran is also expected to learn farming during holidays and harvest.

schoolPressures.label: Transport & safety
schoolPressures.detail: The family will not send Chaitra to PU college by shared auto or cycle on the highway.

schoolPressures.label: Delayed mill payments
schoolPressures.detail: A household waiting on cane payment cannot easily absorb transport, books or uniforms for a second child.

schoolPressures.label: Marriage enquiries
schoolPressures.detail: Relatives have begun informal enquiries about Chaitra's marriage, which become more common once a girl completes secondary school.

female.name: Manjula
female.tagline: A Mandya-born sewing operator stitching export garments while holding up a one-room household in Bengaluru.

dayInLife.text: Cooks the family's meals before leaving for the garment unit.
Walks or takes a short bus ride, free under Shakti, to the northwestern industrial fringe.
Sews through a nine-to-ten-hour shift built around a daily piece-rate quota.
When an export deadline is close, the shift extends and she reaches home after 8 p.m.
Begins a second, unpaid shift of cooking, cleaning and helping her son with schoolwork.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Piece-rate targets, long shifts and a second shift at home
points: She works nine-to-ten-hour shifts at a garment export unit, measured against a daily quota, for close to minimum wage.
Back and shoulder pain and eye strain are managed with painkillers, since piece-rate systems penalise absence.
She knows garment unions and has co-workers in them, but has not joined, fearing supervisor attention and lacking time.

stat.label: Karnataka garment sector statutory minimum wage per month, 2024 study

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: One rented room, shared facilities, and a daughter picking up chores
points: The family rents one room in an unauthorised layout near Peenya, sharing a toilet and water connection with neighbours.
Her husband's construction work is seasonal, so her wage is often the only certain income.
Emergency help comes from neighbouring women in the layout, not relatives; Keerthana minds her brother when shifts run late.

stat.label: Daily housework added to a 9-10 hour factory shift (2024 study)

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Keerthana is at the highest-risk stage: ninth standard
points: Manjula left school after the eighth standard; both children attend a nearby government Kannada-medium school, chosen for cost.
Keerthana faces domestic and sibling-care labour, commuting safety to a distant college, and the pull of garment wages.
Free Shakti bus travel makes a pre-university college plan realistic; Manjula wants Keerthana to finish school first.

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Anaemia risk, joint and eye strain, and costly treatment
points: She has never been diagnosed but recognises the fatigue and breathlessness described, and cannot always afford green vegetables.
Her joint and eye strain from machine stitching goes untreated because a missed factory day costs more than a consultation.
The family relies on the public health centre and government hospital; shared water is blamed for her son's stomach upsets.

stat.label: Anaemia among Bengaluru garment-factory women aged 15 to 49, 2025 study

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Two networks: a Mandya village and neighbouring garment workers
points: Her native village network still guides major decisions, including who her daughter might eventually marry.
Women in her layout, many fellow garment workers, share childcare, lend small sums between paydays and accompany each other late.
She sends money for her village's annual temple festival even when the family cannot attend in person.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: New city corporations, informal housing and welfare that helps in parts
points: Since September 2025 her ward falls under one of five new corporations replacing BBMP; garbage and drainage remain irregular.
Her unauthorised-layout address complicates her BPL ration card, and she has no ESI or provident fund registration.
She is registered to vote in her Mandya village, so she has never voted in a city local election.

stat.label: New city corporations replaced BBMP from September 2025

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Proud of her own wage, frustrated by the cost of living
points: She values supporting the family through her own wage; she blames factory management and global brands for low pay.
She credits Shakti and Anna Bhagya with easing transport and food costs, though they do not address wages.
She wants Keerthana to finish school and find work that avoids ten hours at a machine.

schoolPressures.label: Chores & sibling-care
schoolPressures.detail: When Manjula's shift runs long, Keerthana minds her brother, cooks and does chores, competing with homework.

schoolPressures.label: Commute safety
schoolPressures.detail: The nearest government college is far, and families worry about unsupervised daily travel for a teenage girl.

schoolPressures.label: Factory wages
schoolPressures.detail: Garment work, even at minimum wage, is an immediate income; Keerthana joining her mother is openly discussed.

schoolPressures.label: Missing transfer certificate
schoolPressures.detail: Migrant families who move often fail to carry a transfer certificate, blocking re-enrolment in a new government school.
